text:
anya: Quick sync — I sketched an error-propagation contract for the tri-mode surface; want feedback. TL;DR: we need a deterministic way to surface partial failures (e.g., hosted fallback -> private) without leaking internal stack traces.

ben: +1. Can you paste the contract shape?

anya: Sure, rough idea:
```
{
  code: "ERR_MODEL_TIMEOUT", // stable enum
  phase: "router|adapter|runtime",
  user_facing: "Model timed out, tried fallback variant",
  opaque_details: "opaque-id-12345" // for ops lookup only
}
```

carla: I like phase field. question: do we map hosted fallbacks to the same codes as dedicated? We currently have different error enums.

anya: Proposal: canonical codes at API layer. adapters map internal codes to canonical ones. adapters MUST NOT expose internal stack/hostnames in user_facing.

mike: How should we handle partial outputs? e.g., streamed tokens before an error — we need a way to indicate truncation vs full response.

anya: Add status: "complete|truncated|partial_with_fallback" and optionally `fallback_model` when used.

ben: Ops concern: opaque_details should be stable across retries so logs correlate. That means adapters must attach a trace_id. ok?

anya: Yes. adapters: attach trace_id, and include it in opaque_details. Deploy-bot: last deploy touched adapter translation layer yesterday — any regressions?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T03:22:11 completed to staging. No errors in the translation tests.

carla: One more: rate-limited errors — should they be policy-coded (e.g., THROTTLED_BY_PLAN) vs infra (BACKEND_RATE_LIMIT)? We need both for billing vs user messages.

anya: Split: code and subcode. code is user-level (e.g., THROTTLED), subcode is internal (e.g., AWS_QLIMIT). UI shows code only.

mike: For Private, customers may want raw adapter subcodes in audit logs. We can include subcode in audit but not user_facing.

ben: Agree. Also, consider versioning the contract: add `contract_version` to root so we can evolve without runtime mismatch.

anya: Good call. I'll iterate and post a lightweight RFC with examples and a small conformance checklist for adapters.

carla: Thanks — ping when RFC is up, I'll review the checklist and test harness.

mike: I'll add unit tests in runtime to assert presence of trace_id and status semantics.

anya: Thanks all. End of thread.
